correctness.rationale: Over the reals, \(x^3-y^3=0\) forces \(x=y\), and then \(xz=0\). The nonzero branch has \(z=0\) and reduces separately on \(x>0\) and \(x<0\) to two quadratics with the stated discriminants. Independent symbolic reconstruction of the Jacobian, followed by the equilibrium relation, reproduces the stated cubic. Routh--Hurwitz gives two right-half-plane roots on the positive branch, one on the more-negative branch, and stability on the less-negative branch exactly when \(-3br>1\), equivalent to \(ab>2/9\) within its existence interval.
correctness.risk: At the nondifferentiable equilibrium line ordinary linearization at \(x=0\) is not asserted; the stability classification concerns the isolated smooth equilibria.

final_claim: For \(\dot x=yz,\ \dot y=x^3-y^3,\ \dot z=a|x|-by^3-xy\) with \(a,b>0\), the equilibrium set is the full line \((0,0,z)\), one positive isolated equilibrium for every parameter pair, and additionally two negative isolated equilibria when \(0<4ab<1\) (coalescing at \(4ab=1\)). The isolated-equilibrium characteristic polynomial is \(\lambda^3+3r^2\lambda^2-br^3\lambda+3r^4(1+2br)\); the less-negative branch is asymptotically stable exactly for \(2/9<ab<1/4\), with a zero-Hopf boundary at \(ab=2/9\).
limitations: The hidden-attractor basin condition is not resolved.
